name: Commercial Bank International
founded: 1991 (Emiri Decree No. 5/91 of the Ruler of Ras Al Khaimah, 28 Apr 1991; registered office Ras Al Khaimah, head office Dubai)
ownership_summary: Listed on ADX. Qatar National Bank (QNB) is the largest shareholder with 40% and has four non-independent board seats, including the Vice Chairman. The Bin Owaida family and business hold 22.40% and Mohd Omar Bin Haidar Investment 8.87% (all at 31 Dec 2025). The annual report says the majority of shareholders are UAE citizens and include the Government of Ras Al Khaimah (stake not disclosed). Share capital was unchanged at AED 1,737m from 31 Dec 2024 to 30 Jun 2026, although a rights issue of up to AED 889.1m was approved in Jul 2023. No merger or change of control found for 2024–2026 (official sources checked 2026-10-12).

shareholders.holder: Government of Ras Al Khaimah (named among shareholders; stake below 5%, not disclosed)

government_link: Limited. The annual report says shareholders include the Government of Ras Al Khaimah (below the 5% disclosure threshold) and the bank was set up by Emiri Decree of the Ruler of Ras Al Khaimah. The largest shareholder is Qatar National Bank (40%).
group_structure: Commercial Bank International P.J.S.C. is the bank. It has Cayman SPVs for funding and Tier 1 capital, legacy real-estate subsidiaries from loan resolutions (some partly owned), and CBIx, an innovation and corporate venture-capital arm launched Oct 2025. CBIx Investment Limited and CBIx Tech Labs Limited (DIFC, 100%) first appear as subsidiaries at 30 Jun 2026. An Islamic window still books Islamic financing, but after a CBUAE fine over Islamic-window governance the bank resolved in 2025 to close it in an orderly way, with Higher Shariah Authority no-objection. No wealth, brokerage or asset-management subsidiary found.

subsidiaries.name: CBI Financial Services Limited; CBI Tier 1 Private Ltd (Cayman Islands)

Takamul Real Estate L.L.C. (100%); Al Khaleejiah Property Investments LLC (53%); Al Caribi Development Limited (100%); Callaloo CAY Development Limited (80%, under liquidation); Arzaq Holdings (Private J.S.C.) (48%)

footprint: UAE only: six branches at 30 Jun 2026. The annual report lists locations in Abu Dhabi (Al Bateen Street), Al Ain (electronic banking unit), Dubai (Al Rigga Street, Dubai Mall, Jumeirah Street), Ras Al Khaimah (Julphar Towers) and Sharjah (Al Majaz).
customer_segments: Wholesale Banking Group: mid-market and emerging corporates (150+ new clients in 2025). Innovation Banking: fintech, AI, virtual-asset, tokenisation and gaming firms, plus banking-as-a-service and cards-as-a-service partners. Retail Banking Group: repositioned from mass market to priority and affluent customers (CBI First), with some ultra-high-net-worth clients mentioned.
business_lines: Wholesale banking (FY2025 net operating income AED 453m), retail banking (AED 41m), treasury, real estate (legacy portfolio being sold down), innovation banking / BaaS / cards-as-a-service, and CBIx (innovation lab and corporate venture capital, launched Oct 2025). Reported segments: wholesale banking, retail banking, treasury, real estate, other.

capabilities.wealth_summary: CBI has no visible wealth or investment offer. The personal-banking menu covers accounts, cards, loans, overdraft, savings, insurance and remittance, and the mobile app has no investment features. Its premium offer is CBI First priority banking (accounts, mortgage, loans, CBI First Mastercard, insurance, relationship managers); eligibility thresholds were not on the page fetched. The refreshed strategy (AR 2025) has a pillar 'Build Generational Wealth for Affluent Customers', aiming to grow retail revenue 'by offering a focused Wealth Management proposition powered by select strategic partnerships and a superior CX'. The retail business is small: FY2025 Retail Banking Group net operating income was AED 41m out of AED 791m, with 372 new retail customers in 2025. The bank has an innovation and tokenisation profile: it launched CBIx (Oct 2025), says it advised QNB Wealth and Asset Management and QNB Singapore on a tokenised money market fund (QCD), and is a founding partner in the ASCEND real-world-asset accelerator with Plume.
